plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant five-petaled blossoms on bare branches in late winter. It is widely cultivated in Japan, China, and Korea, and ume plum festivals draw large crowds at this time of year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: East Asia (China, Japan, Korea); cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are a symbol of perseverance in East Asian culture because they bloom in the cold, often while snow is still on the ground.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes through snow and carpets woodlands and gardens in the Northern Hemisphere's late winter.
plants.location: Europe, naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce galantamine, a compound used in medications to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem, a small tree or large shrub with fluffy, ball-shaped, fragrant golden flower clusters and sickle-shaped phyllodes. Some wattles bloom from late winter, and in the Southern Hemisphere summer many other natives are also flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October); some Acacia species flower in other months
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the green and gold of the national sporting colors come from wattle.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers that open in the cooler months. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is popular in gardens in the southeastern United States, Japan, and western Europe.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Japan, Korea, China; cultivated in the southern US, UK, and Mediterranean regions
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea.
